task1.title: How electricity is generated in a hydroelectric power station
task1.prompt: The diagram below shows how electricity is generated in a hydroelectric power station.

chartDesc.title: Hydroelectric power station

stages.label: Water collection in high-level reservoir
stages.detail: River water is collected and stored in a high-level reservoir held back by a dam.

stages.label: Daytime water intake
stages.detail: During the day, the intake gate is opened to allow water to flow down from the high-level reservoir.

stages.label: Daytime electricity generation
stages.detail: Flowing water drives reversible turbines in the power station, which operate a generator.

stages.label: Electricity transmission
stages.detail: Electricity generated is transmitted via power lines to the national grid.

stages.label: Discharge to low-level reservoir
stages.detail: Water passing through the turbines flows into a low-level reservoir.

stages.label: Nighttime pumping cycle
stages.detail: At night, the intake is closed and reversible turbines pump water from the low-level reservoir back up to the high-level reservoir.

chartDesc.overview: The process depicts a reversible hydroelectric power generation system operating on a day and night cycle, generating electricity during the day and pumping water back up to the high-level reservoir at night.
keyFeatures: Cyclical system divided into distinct day and night operations.
Daytime: intake is open, water flows downhill to drive reversible turbines, operate a generator, and send electricity to the national grid.
Nighttime: intake is closed, reversible turbines switch direction to pump water from the low-level reservoir back to the high-level reservoir.

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
